mainTopic: When holy items may be redeemed: blemished animals, impure versus pure מנחות (שמואל and those who argue with him), and items kept from redemption because they are rare.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: nothing made holy in a כלי שרת is ever redeemed. A ברייתא then shows that the תורה calls a blemished animal (בעל מום) 'טמא,' and that only a permanent blemish, not a מום עובר, allows redemption. רב הונא בר מנוח challenges שמואל, who allows pure מנחות and נסכים to be redeemed. He uses the משנה that impure wood, לבונה and כלי שרת cannot be redeemed, arguing that these items still count as 'pure.' The גמרא answers that pure items can be redeemed, and these items are an exception only because they are hard to find. That includes wood, since wood fit for the altar must be free of worms. רב פפא says a ברייתא about unblemished animals given to בדק הבית would have made שמואל retract. The גמרא answers that perfect animals are also rare, so the same reason applies. Next come opposing views: רב כהנא, רבי אושעיא (reported two ways) and רבי אלעזר, who exempts the poor sinner's מנחה based on 'מחטאתו' and 'על חטאתו.' Finally רבי אושעיא reports רבי שמעון's view that a פיגול מנחה cannot become impure as food, and the supporting source continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Items made holy in a service vessel are never redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wraps up the earlier reasoning: we never find that something made holy in a כלי שרת can be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: For we do not find that something sanctified in a service vessel is redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a point from the previous discussion. You cannot compare these items to things that can be redeemed, because nothing holy from a כלי שרת is ever redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being placed in a כלי שרת gives an item a stronger level of holiness. Because the תורה never shows redemption for that level, any comparison to redeemable things like a בעל מום stops working once the item is in the vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: Service vessels of the מקדש that make what is put in them holy
We do not find (there is no known case)
Is redeemed

phrases.english: For from service vessels we do not find
that it is redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the reasoning from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once an item is sanctified in a כלי שרת, it cannot be redeemed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no precedent for redeeming something sanctified in a כלי שרת.

steps.title: Where is a blemished animal called impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a בעל מום is called 'טמא' in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where is a blemished animal called 'impure'?
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier discussion compared impure items to a בעל מום, which is called 'טמא.' Now the גמרא asks where the תורה actually uses that word for a blemished animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished animal is not impure in the usual sense of טומאה. So the גמרא wants a פסוק showing that the word 'טמא' is used for it.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a blemish that makes it unfit for the מזבח
Impure; here possibly meaning 'unfit to be offered'
It is called

phrases.english: And a blemished animal, where
is it called 'impure'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind a claim used in the surrounding discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק where a בעל מום is called טמא.

steps.title: A ברייתא reads the verse as speaking about blemished animals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that 'ואם כל בהמה טמאה' refers to blemished קדשים that can be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'And if it be any impure animal, of which they may not bring an offering to God.' The verse is speaking about blemished animals that are redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. In it, a פסוק that says 'impure animal' is understood to mean a blemished holy animal that may be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'טמאה' here is not about a non-kosher species. It describes an animal that became unfit for the מזבח because of a blemish. That is the source for calling a בעל מום 'טמא.'

keyTerms.meaning: An 'impure animal'; normally a non-kosher species
Are redeemed (exchanged for money so they lose their holiness)
The verse is speaking about

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'And if it be any impure animal
of which they may not bring
an offering to God' –
about blemished animals that are redeemed
the verse is speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means a truly non-kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the פסוק might simply mean a real non-kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it is about blemished animals that were redeemed, or is it only about an actual non-kosher animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own reading. The simple meaning of 'impure animal' is a non-kosher species, so why read it as a blemished animal?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tests whether the non-literal reading is really needed. If the plain meaning works, the ברייתא has no source for calling a בעל מום 'טמא.'

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say (opens a check on a proposed reading)
Or is it only
Actual, literal

phrases.english: Do you say it is about blemished animals that were redeemed,
or is it only
about an actual non-kosher animal?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּבַעֲלֵי מוּמִין שֶׁנִּפְדּוּ אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading given in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why not read 'בהמה טמאה' literally as a non-kosher species?

steps.title: Another verse already covers the non-kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: A later פסוק already covers redeeming a truly non-kosher animal, so 'ואם כל בהמה טמאה' must be about blemished animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says 'And if it be of an impure animal, he shall redeem it according to your valuation,' a non-kosher animal is already mentioned. So how do I explain 'And if it be any impure animal'? The verse is speaking about blemished animals that are redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. A different פסוק already teaches about a real non-kosher animal, so this פסוק must be teaching something else: blemished animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not repeat itself for nothing. Since ויקרא 27:27 already deals with a literal non-kosher animal, the extra mention in 27:11 is applied to a בעל מום.

keyTerms.meaning: When it (the verse) says
According to your valuation
It is already stated
How do I explain (what does this verse come to teach)

steps.whatToRemember: A בעל מום is called 'טמא' because ויקרא 27:11 must be about it. The literal non-kosher animal is already covered in ויקרא 27:27.

phrases.english: When it says
'And if it be of an impure animal
he shall redeem it according to your valuation,'
a non-kosher animal is already stated.
So how do I explain
'And if it be any impure animal'?
About blemished animals that are redeemed
the verse is speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״וְאִם בַּבְּהֵמָה הַטְּמֵאָה וּפָדָה בְעֶרְכֶּךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 and confirms the reading of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 27:27 already covers a literal non-kosher animal, so 27:11 refers to a בעל מום.

steps.title: Can a temporary blemish allow redemption?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether an animal with a מום עובר could also be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think they can be redeemed even because of a temporary blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now asks how far this rule goes. Can a holy animal with a blemish that will heal also be redeemed? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that blemished animals can be redeemed, the question is which blemishes count. A temporary blemish leaves the animal unfit only for now.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought
A temporary blemish that will go away

phrases.english: One might think they are redeemed
because of a temporary blemish?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the limits of the rule set in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a מום עובר also allow redemption?

steps.title: Only an animal that can never be offered is redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The words 'אשר לא יקריבו ממנה קרבן לה׳' exclude an animal with a temporary blemish, since it can be offered later.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'of which they may not bring an offering to God.' This means an animal that is not offered to God at all. It excludes this one, which is not offered today but is offered tomorrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the words of the same פסוק. Only an animal that can never go on the מזבח may be redeemed, and that rules out a temporary blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They may not bring an offering' is read as a permanent state. An animal with a מום עובר will become fit again once it heals, so it keeps its holiness and cannot be redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse comes to teach
At all
Is excluded

steps.whatToRemember: Only a מום קבוע (permanent blemish) allows a holy animal to be redeemed. A מום עובר does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical הלכה that redemption of קדשים depends on a lasting blemish, not a temporary one.

phrases.english: The verse teaches
'of which they may not bring an offering to God' –
one that is not offered to God
at all,
excluding this one, which is not offered today
but is offered tomorrow.
phrases.notes: He means an animal whose blemish will heal, so it can go on the מזבח later.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קׇרְבָּן לַה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מום עובר does not allow redemption. Only an animal that can never be offered may be redeemed.

steps.title: רב הונא בר מנוח quotes a teaching about impure holy items
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר מנוח opens an objection by quoting a teaching: birds, wood, לבונה and כלי שרת that became טמא cannot be redeemed, because פדיון is only mentioned for an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר מנוח raised an objection: Birds, wood, frankincense, and service vessels that became impure cannot be redeemed, because the תורה mentions redemption only for an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins. רב הונא בר מנוח quotes a teaching that he will use to attack an earlier opinion, and the גמרא is setting up the argument that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching lists four kinds of holy items that became טמא and says none can be redeemed. The stated reason is that the תורה only allows פדיון for an animal. On its own this sounds simple, but רב הונא בר מנוח will press on why it applies to all four items.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption: exchanging a holy item for money so the item loses its holiness
The holy vessels used for service in the בית המקדש
Frankincense, burned on the מזבח
They became ritually impure

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Manoach raised an objection:
Birds, wood, frankincense, and service vessels
that became impure have no redemption,
for redemption was stated only about an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that פדיון is said only about a blemished animal, and uses it to open a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view (שמואל's) that pure מנחות and נסכים can be redeemed before they are sanctified in a כלי שרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The quoted teaching will show that the real reason these items are not redeemed is that 'pure' holy items are never redeemed.

steps.title: Birds make sense, but why not redeem wood, frankincense and vessels?
steps.stepSummary: Birds cannot be redeemed because they have קדושת הגוף and are not animals. But wood, לבונה and כלי שרת lack that holiness, so the real reason must be that pure holy items are never redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Birds are understandable: they have inherent holiness, and redemption was said only for an animal. But wood, frankincense, and service vessels should be redeemable! So isn't the reason that pure holy items in general are not redeemed?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר מנוח explains why the teaching is a problem. He shows that the stated reason only fits birds, so a different reason must explain the other three items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Items with קדושת הגוף can only be redeemed if the תורה allows it, and the תורה only allows it for an animal, so birds are excluded. Wood, לבונה and כלי שרת don't have that kind of holiness, so that reason doesn't stop them. He concludes the real rule is: holy items that are pure are not redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense regarding..., used before raising a problem
Holiness on the item itself, not just on its money value
Let them be redeemed
Rather, isn't it that... introduces the conclusion the challenger wants to prove

phrases.english: Granted, birds have inherent holiness,
and redemption was stated only about an animal.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עֵצִים וּלְבוֹנָה וּכְלֵי שָׁרֵת – לִיפַּרְקוּ?
phrases.english: But wood, frankincense, and service vessels: let them be redeemed!
Rather, isn't it because
pure holy items in general are not redeemed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the quoted teaching and draws the inference that powers the objection.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that pure holy items without קדושת הגוף, like מנחות before being placed in a כלי שרת, can be redeemed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the 'only an animal' reason can't explain wood, לבונה and כלי שרת, the only remaining reason is that pure items are never redeemed. That contradicts allowing pure מנחות to be redeemed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the heart of the objection: it turns a list of items into a general rule against redeeming anything that is pure.

steps.title: Why these impure items still count as pure
steps.stepSummary: Even though these items became טמא, they are treated like pure items, because wood and לבונה are not normally food and only become able to receive טומאה through חיבת הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these items too, even though they became impure, are like pure items. Wood and frankincense are not things that can become food; it is only the special regard for holiness that treats them like food.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenger heads off the obvious reply: 'But the teaching is about impure items!' He explains that their impurity is weak, so they still count as pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only food, vessels and similar things can become טמא, and wood or לבונה are not food. They can only become טמא because of חיבת הקודש, a special rule for holy things. Since their טומאה comes only from this extra rule, they are still treated like pure items for the question of redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: They are like pure items
Food; things in the food category can become טמא
The special regard for holy things, which makes them able to become טמא even when they normally couldn't

steps.confusionAlert: The teaching really does talk about items that became טמא. The point here is that their impurity is a weak, special kind, so for redemption they are still counted as pure.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי נָמֵי, אַף עַל גַּב דְּנִטְמְאוּ –
phrases.english: And these too, even though they became impure,
are like pure items,
because wood and frankincense
are not things that can be made into food,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא חִיבַּת הַקּוֹדֶשׁ מַשְׁוֵה לְהוּ אוּכְלָא.
phrases.english: rather, the regard for holiness makes them count as food.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי נָמֵי, אַף עַל גַּב דְּנִטְמְאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the objection by explaining why items listed as impure can still be called 'pure'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The same view that pure holy items can be redeemed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blocks the escape that the teaching is only about truly impure items, so the rule 'pure items are not redeemed' still stands.

steps.title: Details: wood, frankincense and vessels have only limited impurity
steps.stepSummary: Wood can't become טמא until it is cut into logs, לבונה until it is sanctified in a כלי שרת, and כלי שרת can be purified in a מקוה. So all three are weakly impure and count as pure, completing the objection.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wood, as long as it is not trimmed into logs, cannot become impure. Frankincense too, as long as it is not sanctified in a service vessel, cannot become impure. Service vessels too, since they can become pure in a מקוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenger gives the specific reason for each item to show why its טומאה is weak. This finishes the objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood and לבונה only become able to receive טומאה at a late stage, and only because of חיבת הקודש. כלי שרת do become טמא, but a מקוה can fix that, so the טומאה is not permanent. All three count as 'pure', so the teaching proves pure holy items are not redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: Logs: wood trimmed and cut for the מזבח
Become able to receive טומאה
Made holy by being placed in a כלי שרת
Becoming pure by immersing in a מקוה

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא בר מנוח's objection: a teaching says impure wood, לבונה and כלי שרת cannot be redeemed. Since their impurity is weak and they count as pure, the real rule must be that pure holy items are never redeemed. That challenges the view that pure מנחות can be redeemed.

phrases.aramaic: דְּעֵצִים, כַּמָּה דְּלָא מְשַׁפֵּי לְהוּ לִגְזִירִין –
phrases.english: For wood, as long as one has not trimmed it into logs,
it cannot become impure.

phrases.aramaic: לְבוֹנָה נָמֵי, כַּמָּה דְּלָא קָידְשָׁה בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת –
phrases.english: Frankincense too, as long as it was not sanctified in a service vessel,
it cannot become impure.
Service vessels too
count as pure, since they can become pure in a mikveh.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּעֵצִים, כַּמָּה דְּלָא מְשַׁפֵּי לְהוּ לִגְזִירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out for each item why its impurity is weak, finishing the objection begun in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that pure holy items, like מנחות not yet sanctified in a כלי שרת, can be redeemed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since all three items count as pure and the teaching says they cannot be redeemed, pure holy items cannot be redeemed.

steps.title: Pure items can be redeemed; these items are a special case because they are hard to find
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the objection by saying pure items generally can be redeemed. Wood, לבונה and כלי שרת are not redeemed only because they are not commonly available.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, I will tell you that pure items in general can be redeemed. These particular items are not redeemed only because they are hard to find.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the objection from steps 8 to 11 and saves the idea that pure items can be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection said these items cannot be redeemed because they are pure. The answer gives a different reason: they are rare. If people could redeem them, the בית המקדש might run short of them, so this is a special exception and not a general rule about pure items.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I will tell you. This introduces a defense of the original position.
Pure items
Are redeemed
They are not commonly found or available

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer creates the idea of 'not commonly available' as a reason for a special rule. The rest of this section depends on that idea.

phrases.english: No, really I will tell you:
pure items in general are redeemed,
and these are not redeemed because they are not commonly available.
phrases.notes: 'These' means the wood, לבונה and כלי שרת from the משנה quoted in step 8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection that steps 8 to 11 built up.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason for the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: These items are not redeemed because pure holy items are never redeemed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pure items can be redeemed. These items are an exception because they are rare.

steps.title: Wood is easy to find, so why can't it be redeemed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that לבונה and כלי שרת are rare. It points out that wood is easy to find.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that לבונה and כלי שרת are hard to find. But wood is very easy to find!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new answer on wood, which seems to be everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 12 depends on all three items being rare. Wood looks like a weak spot, because the 'rare' reason does not seem to fit it.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense. This accepts one part before challenging another.
Wood (for burning on the מזבח)
They are very commonly found

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְבוֹנָה וּכְלֵי שָׁרֵת – לָא שְׁכִיחִי,
phrases.english: Granted, frankincense and service vessels are not commonly available,
but wood is very commonly found!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְבוֹנָה וּכְלֵי שָׁרֵת – לָא שְׁכִיחִי, אֶלָּא עֵצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that all three items are 'not commonly available'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wood is everywhere, so the rarity reason cannot explain why wood is not redeemed.

steps.title: Wood fit for the altar is also hard to find
steps.stepSummary: Any wood with a worm in it is disqualified for the מזבח. So wood good enough for the altar is not common.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wood is also rare. The Master said that any wood with a worm in it is disqualified for the מזבח. So good wood is not easy to find.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that wood fit for the altar is actually rare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary wood is common, but the מזבח needs worm-free wood, and that is much harder to find. So the 'not commonly available' reason applies to wood too, and the answer from step 12 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A worm
Disqualified
Therefore

phrases.english: Wood too is not common,
since the Master said:
any wood in which a worm is found
is disqualified for the altar,
therefore it is not commonly available.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about wood in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the category: only wood fit for the altar counts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wood is common, so the rarity reason does not apply to it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Worm-free wood fit for the altar is rare, so the rarity reason does apply.
steps.whatToRemember: Wood, לבונה and כלי שרת are not redeemed because they are hard to get, not because pure items can never be redeemed.

steps.title: רב פפא: a ברייתא about unblemished animals would have made שמואל change his mind
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings a ברייתא: unblemished animals given to בדק הבית can only be redeemed for the מזבח. Even though they have only monetary holiness, they cannot be redeemed because they are pure. He says שמואל would have taken back his view if he had known it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If שמואל had heard this ברייתא, he would have taken back his view. The ברייתא says: Someone who gives unblemished animals to בדק הבית cannot redeem them except for use on the מזבח. This is because anything fit for the מזבח never leaves the מזבח. So even though they only have holiness of value, they are not redeemed, since they are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks שמואל's view with a ברייתא. In that ברייתא, items with only monetary holiness still cannot be redeemed, and the reason seems to be that they are pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said pure items with only monetary holiness can be redeemed. The ברייתא seems to say the opposite: these animals have only קדושת דמים, yet they cannot be redeemed because they are pure. That looks like a direct contradiction to שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: One who consecrates (sets something aside as holy)
Unblemished animals, fit to be offered
The fund for upkeep of the בית המקדש
Holiness of monetary value only, not holiness of the item's body
He retracted, took back his view

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
If Shmuel had heard
that which is taught in a baraita:
one who consecrates unblemished animals for Temple maintenance,
they are redeemed only for the altar,
because anything that is fit for the altar
never leaves the altar's domain,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דִּקְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים נִינְהוּ –
phrases.english: and even though they have only sanctity of value,
they are not redeemed, since they are pure,
he would have retracted his view.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי שְׁמִיעָא לֵיהּ לִשְׁמוּאֵל הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge to שמואל from a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that pure items with only קדושת דמים can be redeemed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says items with only monetary holiness are not redeemed because they are pure, which contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: שמואל knew the ברייתא and explained it as a 'not commonly available' case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב פפא's claim. שמואל knew the ברייתא and did not change his mind, because he explains it with the same rarity reason used earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not so. שמואל heard this ברייתא and did not take back his view. Didn't you say there that since these items are not commonly available, they are not redeemed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away רב פפא's challenge and says שמואל can keep his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא explained that some items are not redeemed only because they are rare, and not because they are pure. שמואל can read the ברייתא the same way, as a special rule about availability. So it does not prove that pure items are never redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so. This rejects the previous claim.
There, in the earlier case
They are redeemed

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's view holds: pure items with only monetary holiness can normally be redeemed. Any case where they are not redeemed is explained as a special rule, because those items are hard to get.

phrases.english: But that is not so;
he heard it and did not retract.
Didn't you say there:
phrases.notes: 'There' points back to step 12, about wood, לבונה and כלי שרת.

phrases.english: since they are not commonly available, they are not redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, שְׁמִיעָא לֵיהּ וְלָא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא would have forced שמואל to retract
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be explained by the rarity reason, so it does not show that purity blocks redemption.

steps.title: Unblemished animals are also rare, because blemishes are so common
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies the rarity reason to animals. So many small blemishes disqualify an animal that a perfect one is hard to find.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too: blemishes that disqualify an animal are common. Even a mark on the eyeball disqualifies it. So unblemished animals are not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining how שמואל reads the ברייתא of רב פפא. Unblemished animals are like the altar wood: something fit for the מזבח is hard to find.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said wood is rare because any worm disqualifies it. Now it says the same about animals: even a tiny blemish in the eye makes an animal unfit. Since perfect animals are rare, חז"ל did not let them be redeemed for ordinary use. This does not apply to flour and wine, which are easy to find.

keyTerms.meaning: Blemishes that make an animal unfit to be a קרבן
Small marks or spots on the eyeball, which still count as a blemish
Common, easy to find

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל keeps his view: pure מנחות and נסכים can be redeemed. The cases where pure items are not redeemed (wood, לבונה, כלי שרת, unblemished animals) are all things that are hard to find.

phrases.english: Here too,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the ברייתא רב פפא brought, about unblemished animals given to בדק הבית.

phrases.english: since blemishes that disqualify an animal are common,
for even marks on the eyeball also disqualify,
therefore they (unblemished animals) are not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the rarity reason that step 16 said שמואל uses for the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same reason as before: the item is rare
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seems to show that anything pure, even with only monetary holiness, cannot be redeemed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only rare items fit for the מזבח are not redeemed. Unblemished animals are rare because blemishes are common.

steps.title: רב כהנא and רבי אושעיא: only impure ones are redeemed
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא disagrees with שמואל. Impure מנחות and נסכים may be redeemed, but pure ones may not. רבי אושעיא says the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: impure ones are redeemed, pure ones are not redeemed. רבי אושעיא said the same: impure ones are redeemed, pure ones are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings an opinion that argues with שמואל. רב כהנא, along with רבי אושעיא, does not allow pure מנחות to be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל allowed even pure מנחות and נסכים to be redeemed, as long as they were not yet placed in a כלי שרת. רב כהנא allows redemption only when they became impure and can no longer be offered. If they are still pure, they must be brought as a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure, so they can no longer be offered
Pure, still fit to be offered
Are redeemed (their holiness moves onto money)

steps.confusionAlert: This is the opposite of שמואל's view. For שמואל pure ones are redeemed too. For רב כהנא only impure ones are.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
Impure ones are redeemed,
pure ones are not redeemed.
And so said Rabbi Oshaya:
Impure ones are redeemed,
pure ones are not redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the defense of שמואל, the גמרא brings an opinion that argues with him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only impure מנחות and נסכים may be redeemed. Pure ones may not.

steps.title: Another version: רבי אושעיא says even pure ones are redeemed
steps.stepSummary: Some report רבי אושעיא's view differently. In this version, even pure מנחות are redeemed, like שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רבי אושעיא said: even pure ones are redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second report of what רבי אושעיא held. In this report he agrees with שמואל instead of רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two reports disagree about whose side רבי אושעיא is on. In the first he sides with רב כהנא. In this one he says even pure items can be redeemed, which matches שמואל.

phrases.english: There are those who say that Rabbi Oshaya said:
Even pure ones are redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different report of רבי אושעיא's view than the one in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, even pure מנחות and נסכים are redeemed.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: pure ones are not redeemed, except the poor sinner's flour offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר agrees that pure מנחות are not redeemed. He makes one exception: the עשירית האיפה of a מנחת חוטא, which is redeemed even when pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: all of them, if impure, are redeemed; if pure, are not redeemed. The exception is the tenth of an איפה of the מנחת חוטא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר states a general rule like רב כהנא, then adds one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His basic rule is that only impure מנחות are redeemed. But the מנחת חוטא, the flour offering of a very poor person who sinned, can be redeemed even while pure. The next step gives his reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה; the measure of flour used for the מנחה
The flour offering a very poor person brings for certain sins (part of the קרבן עולה ויורד)
Except for

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
All of them, if impure, are redeemed,
phrases.notes: "All of them" means all the kinds of מנחות.

phrases.english: if pure, are not redeemed,
except for the tenth of an ephah
of a sinner's meal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: כּוּלָּן טְמֵאִין – נִפְדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third view. It agrees with רב כהנא's basic rule but adds one exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pure מנחות are not redeemed, except the עשירית האיפה of a מנחת חוטא, which is redeemed even when pure.

steps.title: The Torah's wording, "מחטאתו" and "על חטאתו", is the source for the exception
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר's exception comes from two different phrasings the תורה uses about this sin offering: "מחטאתו" and "על חטאתו".
steps.simpleTranslation: For the Torah said: "from his sin" and "for his sin".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for רבי אלעזר's exception. It points to two different words the תורה uses about this offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה describes the קרבן עולה ויורד with two different phrasings, "מחטאתו" and "על חטאתו". The גמרא reads the difference as a hint. If a poor person set aside his flour and then became rich, he may redeem the flour even though it is pure, and add money to buy the richer person's offering. That is why this one מנחה is redeemed even when pure.

keyTerms.meaning: "From his sin"; one of the Torah's phrasings for this offering
"For his sin"; another phrasing. עַל can also mean "on top of", hinting at adding more

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows why the מנחת חוטא is different from other מנחות. The person bringing it may move up to a richer offering, so his flour must be able to be redeemed even while pure.

phrases.english: For the Torah said:
"From his sin"
phrases.notes: Both phrasings come from ויקרא פרק ה, about the קרבן עולה ויורד.

phrases.english: "For his sin."
phrases.notes: The גמרא only hints at the lesson here. The idea is that a poor person who became rich can redeem his flour and add money for a bigger offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the Torah source for the exception רבי אלעזר made in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's exception: the עשירית האיפה of a מנחת חוטא is redeemed even when pure.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah's two phrasings, "מחטאתו" and "על חטאתו", in ויקרא פרק ה.

steps.title: A פיגול meal offering does not become impure as food
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא reports a tradition: according to רבי שמעון, a מנחה that became פיגול cannot become impure the way food does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: I heard that according to רבי שמעון, a meal offering that became פיגול does not become impure with the impurity of food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement. רבי אושעיא passes on something he heard about how רבי שמעון treats a פיגול מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally food can become impure if it touches something impure. רבי אושעיא says that in רבי שמעון's view, a מנחה that became פיגול is an exception: it cannot become impure as food at all. The גמרא will now show where this idea comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering ruined by the intent, during the service, to eat it after its allowed time
The kind of impurity that food can receive
I heard; he is passing on a tradition he received

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
I heard that one who made a meal offering piggul,
phrases.notes: פיגול means the offering was brought with the plan to eat it after its allowed time, which ruins it.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi Shimon,
it is not susceptible to the impurity of food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of redeeming pure and impure מנחות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, a מנחה that became פיגול cannot receive טומאת אוכלין.

steps.title: The source begins: ערלה and כלאי הכרם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting the teaching that backs up רבי אושעיא's report, opening with ערלה and כלאי הכרם.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: ערלה and כלאי הכרם...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting a source to support רבי אושעיא. The quote is not finished yet; it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source starts by listing ערלה and כלאי הכרם, foods that are forbidden for any use. The point of the quote, which comes next, will be how רבי שמעון rules about such foods and impurity. רבי אושעיא's report about פיגול is built on that ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit from a tree's first three years, which is forbidden
Forbidden mixtures of grain or vegetables planted in a vineyard
Something you may not use or benefit from at all

phrases.english: As we learned: Orla and diverse kinds in a vineyard,
phrases.notes: The list keeps going on the next amud, where the actual ruling appears.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that supports רבי אושעיא's statement in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אושעיא's claim that, according to רבי שמעון, a פיגול מנחה does not receive טומאת אוכלין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching that lists ערלה and כלאי הכרם (it continues on the next amud).
